thread.title: Apple buys Next Issue Media

author: Anthony Noto
title: Apple buys Next Issue Media
text: – Reporter, New York Business Journal Mar 12, 2018, 2:47pm CDT Apple Inc . is acquiring Next Issue Media LLC from private equity firm KKR & Co. Terms of the deal remain undisclosed. New York-based KKR (NYSE: KKR) invested $50 million in Next Issue in December 2014. The news was announced on the Apple website . Next Issue Media is known for giving users unlimited access to their favorite magazine titles through its monthly, multi-title subscription service, Texture. The service brings more than 200 magazines from around the globe to life, providing an easy way for users to read all or part of their favorite titles. “We’re excited Texture will join Apple, along with an impressive catalog of magazines from many of the world’s leading publishers,” said Eddy Cue , Apple’s senior vice president of Internet Software and Services. “We are committed to quality journalism from trusted sources and allowing magazines to keep producing beautifully designed and engaging stories for users.” “I’m thrilled that Next Issue Media, and its award-winning Texture app, are being acquired by Apple,” said CEO of Next Issue Media John Loughlin. “The Texture team and its current owners, Condé Nast, Hearst, Meredith , Rogers Media and KKR, could not be more pleased or excited with this development. We could not imagine a better home or future for the service.” Texture launched in 2010 from a consortium of publishers, including Hearst, News Corp. (Nasdaq: NWS), Meredith Corp. (NYSE: MDP) and Condé Nast, a sister company to The Business Journals. It went on to become Next Issue Media’s flagship product. In 2016, the service was chosen by the App Store editorial team for the annual Best Of selections, which celebrate the most innovative apps and games for iOS users. The deal comes at a time when Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) races against Google in a quest to take over innovative startups especially when it comes to artificial intelligence. According to VentureBeat , Google leads the way with 14 acquisitions. Its most recent target — Banter — helps businesses connect with their customers over popular messaging platforms like Facebook Messenger, Twitter and Snapchat. – Reporter, New York Business Journal Mar 12, 2018, 2:47pm CDT Related Content
